cues.text: Hello.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Hi, is that Tanya?
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Yes ... Simon ... lovely to hear you! How are you?
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Very well ... and we’re so looking forward to seeing you.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: So am I.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Now I don’t have a lot of time, I’m afraid, so I wanted to make sure we’ve got all your details. Have you confirmed your flights?
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Yes I’m definitely coming on the twenty second of June.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Excellent. Have you got your flight number?
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Not with me, I’m afraid, but I promise I’ll email it ... let me make a note of all this.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Yes, do, because one of us’ll try to come and collect you from the airport, if we can.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: I presume you’ll be coming into Terminal One?
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Aggh ... I don’t know ... I’ll have to find out which one it is ...
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Yes ... you must ... we don’t want to be waiting at the wrong one!
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: But hang on ... I’ll be arriving at about lunch time ... and that’ll mean you have to take time off work to pick me up. You really mustn’t do that.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Look ... we’re not all that busy at work and if there’s a problem I can text you when you arrive and you can take a taxi.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: OK .
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: There’s a really good company called Q2 Pantera.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Can you spell that?
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: It’s P-A-N-T-E-R-A. They have a stand at the airport ... you can’t miss it ... and they’re really reliable.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Great, thanks ... how far are you from the airport?
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: About forty minutes.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: And you’re near the city centre, aren’t you?
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: We’re East of it actually ... don’t tell the driver city centre because you’ll really get caught up in traffic!
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: OK! And I’ll make sure I carry your address with me. Now have you got my mobile ... um ... cell phone number?
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Yes, you sent it last month.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: But I tell you what ... I don’t think I’ve got yours ... I’d better have it now, just in case.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: OK ... and I changed it recently anyway. Ready? It’s Q4 zero seven seven six five, three two eight, four double one.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Thanks. Now, what should I pack ... ?
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Well, all the usual ... casual clothes mainly. Though you’d better bring an evening dress. We’ll be having at least one fancy dinner at a Q5 hotel restaurant.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Now, when you’re coming, unfortunately the weather’s not going to be brilliant.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: I know, it’s the rainy season ... I’m bringing an umbrella.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: We have tons of those ... so don’t pack one, but pack a Q6 raincoat. a good one ‘cause we’ll try and get out for plenty of hikes.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: OK, sure. Sounds super ... just what I love. And I’d better remember to pack my sturdy walking Q7 shoes.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Excellent idea ... it’s pretty rugged round here ... so they have to be tough!
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: I can imagine. I’m so looking forward to getting out. Oh Simon, before I forget, you recommended I read a book about your area .
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Yeah.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: What was the name again? I’d like to read it ... to get an idea of the history, etc.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: It’s called ‘ Q8 Mountain Lives’ and it’s ...
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Hang on ... I’m just writing it down ... OK.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: ... and it’s by Rex Campbell.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Great, I’ll try and get hold of that.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Well worth it.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Now the really important things are gifts.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Oh don’t worry about that . just bring yourself .
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: I know but I’d like to get something for your parents. What about Janice ... I know she loves English tea.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: That’s very kind ... but she’s not drinking so much of that these days. But she’d love some chocolate ... you know her favourite.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Oh yes ... that’d be nice ... I’ll do that. And Alec? Is he still into racing?
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Very much so.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: I was thinking of bringing a calendar ... you know, with horse-racing pictures.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: What a good idea ... he’d love that ...
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Great . so that’s about it I think.
cues.speaker: Tanya

cues.text: Yes, I think so . so you’ll send me your number
cues.speaker: Simon
